decisions.reason: Although launched from the firm's sustainability platform, a vegan superfood drink mix is commercially and organizationally much farther from its core industrial process, engineering and B2B capabilities, so absorptive capacity and learning advantages are weaker and management would likely reallocate resources.

Modular waste-to-energy plant extensions sit squarely inside the firm's established engineering and waste-to-energy knowledge base, where its in-house R&D and research links give strong capacity to interpret early results and improve the product.

A waste-oil-to-energy plant closely matches the firm's existing technological competences and was given dedicated presentation after launch, suggesting enough strategic fit and learning potential for management to continue rather than exit.

Plastic-waste-to-fuel is adjacent to the firm's core waste-conversion activities and benefits from its research intensity, but the technology and commercialization risk are higher than for more incremental extensions, so it is kept with somewhat greater review risk.
